name: Access0x1Hook
description: Open receipts for swaps. A swap that carries a payee and an order reference as hookData leaves one Receipt event with the amounts the swap actually moved, for any payee but the empty one. It never reverts a swap, moves no funds, returns no delta, and has no owner and no list of payees.

reasons: No dynamic fee and no returns-delta flag.
A swap with empty hookData goes through and leaves no receipt; a receipt needs a caller that sends the hookData.
The 0x91 address-prefix rule applies to a deployed address. This hook is not deployed.

pool.binding: None. Any pool may name this hook; each PoolId has its own receipts.
pool.fee: Any. The hook does not read or set the fee.

deltas.settledBy: Nobody. Without the afterSwapReturnDelta bit the PoolManager does not read the value.

externalCalls.target: the one router named at deployment
externalCalls.why: Only this address is asked who the swapper is. In try/catch: a router that reverts means nobody is recognised.

securityAssumptions: Assumes the v4 `PoolManager` is the only caller of the callbacks (enforced by the `onlyPoolManager` modifier inherited from `BaseHook`).
Assumes the router named at deployment answers `msgSender()` with the account that called it. A router that lies makes every statement here about 'the swapper' false.
doesNotGuarantee: Does not say where a swap's output went: that is the router's choice, and a hook with this mask cannot see or control it.
Does not write a receipt for a swap routed without hookData, which is every swap from a general interface.
Does not establish the payer for a swap that did not come through the router named at deployment: the payer on such a receipt is empty.
Does not restrict which pools use it. Anyone can initialise a pool that names this hook.
Does not say that a payee id means anything: any 32 bytes but zero are accepted.

invariants.statement: The hook's address carries exactly the permissions it declares: afterSwap, mask 0x40.
The constructor rejects an address with one bit different.
A swap naming a payee leaves exactly one receipt, recorded under the swapper the router reported.
A swap with no hookData writes nothing, and an empty payee is refused a receipt while the swap goes through.
Whatever bytes are sent as hookData, the swap goes through.
